pageCache.pageTitle: City of London Academy Highgate Hill - Altruism. Respect. Tenacity.
pageCache.text:
At City of London Academy Highgate Hill, we believe that all students can thrive in their academic lives and become active contributors to their local, national and global communities, if the right environment is provided. We aim to provide a world class education for our students – making them ‘well-rounded’ individuals. Hence we provide a broad and balanced curriculum tailored to the needs of our students.
We strive to provide a calm and purposeful learning environment underpinned by high expectations across the academy. We provide opportunities through high quality teaching and support to promote academic, creative, sporting, linguistic and personal achievement: this is ‘the City experience’.
We believe that you will be impressed by the outstanding educational experiences we can offer and encourage you to visit the academy to find out more. Our aim is to make the transition from primary to secondary education as smooth as possible. We have spaces available. Get in touch to find out more.

pageCache.pageTitle: Principal's welcome - City of London Academy Highgate Hill
pageCache.text:
Principal’s welcome
A warm welcome from our Principal, Prince Gennuh
It is my pleasure to welcome you to City of London Academy Highgate Hill.
The school opened as a mixed, all-ability, non-denominational academy in September 2017, from what was previously Mount Carmel Catholic College for Girls. The academy is housed in a lovely building with excellent facilities for students, staff and the community. We aim to provide a world class education for our students – making them ‘well-rounded’ individuals. Hence we provide a broad and balanced curriculum tailored to the needs of our students. This includes the opportunity for students to achieve the ‘English Baccalaureate’ (EBacc).
At City of London Academy Highgate Hill, we believe that all students can thrive in their academic lives and become active contributors to their local, national and global communities, if the right environment is provided. Therefore, we strive to provide a calm and purposeful learning environment underpinned by high expectations across the academy. Students are expected to work hard and show tenacity and commitment towards their studies. We provide opportunities through high quality teaching and support structures offered by our sponsor: the City of London Corporation, to promote academic, creative, sporting, linguistic and personal achievement: this is ‘the City experience’.
The academy’s sixth form, Islington Collegiate Sixth Form (ICS), launched in September 2022, and we opened our new state of the art building in 2023. ICS aims to inspire and lead its students to achieve their highest goals, whilst encouraging them to be articulate and intellectually curious young adults who are committed to mastering their subjects. Through a scholarly environment ICS guides its students so they have the skills and knowledge to thrive at highly competitive academic destinations in the world, including Oxbridge and Ivy League universities.
I feel extremely privileged to lead this wonderful academy with our enthusiastic students, diligent staff, supportive parents/carers and cohesive Local Board.
You are welcome to book an appointment to visit the academy where I would be more than happy to meet with you. Please email: enquiries@highgatehill.cola.org.uk
Prince GennuhPrincipal

pageCache.pageTitle: Year 9 Options - City of London Academy Highgate Hill
pageCache.text:
Year 9 Options
Welcome to the Year 9 Options information page for courses starting in September 2023. The information contained will help you, alongside the people who know you best: your parents/carers, head of year and subject teachers, to make the best possible decisions about which subjects to study over the next two years.
This is an exciting, promising time for young men/women entering professional life. By choosing the right courses now, your child will equip themselves with the skills, knowledge and aptitudes required for the career or careers of their choice, even while their ideas about this are evolving. All of our staff are available to offer guidance and support in making these important decisions. All the courses require determination, dedication and enthusiasm.
KS4 is NOT about collecting as many GCSEs or Btecs as you can, the quality of your qualification is far more important. Universities (if you are considering applying later) are more impressed with grades than the number of subjects taken. Employers are more impressed with how relevant and useful your subjects are, rather than how many you have!
Everyone knows that qualifications are not the only things needed for success in life – common sense, reliability, a willingness to learn, team spirit, communication skills, leadership qualities, time management, personal organisation and initiative are also key to your success. Remember that although this process is important, it is not the end of your learning and there are many different roads to achieve the success that you deserve.
Below you will see the presentation that was given during our Year 9 Options Evening, along with a copy of the Year 9 Options Booklet. On the sub-page, you will find copies of the subject presentations from the Options Evening.
Mrs Didsbury Taylor – Assistant Principal

pageCache.pageTitle: Exam results - City of London Academy Highgate Hill
pageCache.text:
Exam results
Raising academic standards at Highgate Hill
Key stage 4 performance in 2025
Progress 8 score
The DfE was not able to calculate Progress 8 scores for academic years 2024/25 and 2025/26. This is because there was no KS2 assessment data available to calculate the baseline for Progress 8 for these years due to Covid-19 disruption.
Attainment 8
Schools get a score based on how well pupils have performed in up to 8 qualifications.
This score is based on up to 8 qualifications including English, maths, three English Baccalaureate qualifications including sciences, computer science, history, geography and languages, and three other additional approved qualifications.
In 2025 our pupils achieved an Attainment 8 score of 40.3.
Staying in education or entering employment
This shows the number of pupils who either stayed in education or went into employment after finishing key stage 4 (after year 11, usually aged 16).
GCSEs are graded 1 (low) to 9 (high). Grade 5 is a similar level of achievement to a high grade C or low grade B in the old grading.
89% of our pupils stayed in education or entered employment after finishing key stage 4, compared with 91% nationally.
Grade 5 or above in English and maths GCSEs
The percentage of pupils who achieved grade 5 or above in English and maths GCSEs combined.
GCSEs are graded 1 (low) to 9 (high). Grade 5 is a similar level of achievement to a high grade C or low grade B in the old grading.
In 2025 33% of pupils achieved grade 5 or above in English and maths GCSEs.
Entering EBacc
A pupil is considered to have entered for the English Baccalaureate if they entered for qualifications in English, maths, sciences, a language and either history or geography.
In 2025, 44.3% of pupils entered the English Baccalaureate.
EBacc average point score (APS)
The EBacc average points score calculates a pupil’s average point scores across the five pillars of the English Baccalaureate.
In 2025 our pupils achieved an EBacc average point score of 3.64.

pageCache.pageTitle: Pupil Premium - City of London Academy Highgate Hill
pageCache.text:
Pupil Premium
What is the Pupil Premium Grant?
The Pupil Premium Grant (PPG) is additional funding given to schools to raise the attainment of disadvantaged pupils, and to close the gap between the highest and lowest achieving pupilsnationally. Pupil Premium support is also directed towards supporting children and young people with parents in the regular armed forces. Disadvantaged pupils in Years 7 to 11 recorded as Ever6 FSM receive £955.00 per pupil. Children adopted from care, or who have left care (referred to as post-LAC), receive £2345.00 per pupil.
To find out more, visit the What You Need to Know guide on the Department for Education website.
Pupil Premium strategy
Pupil Premium funding is allocated to City of London Academy Highgate Hill based on the number of pupils in its secondary year groups who are eligible for deprivation, i.e. Free School Meals (FSM) or Looked After Children (LAC). Up to 60% of our students meet this criteria.
Main barriers to academic achievement faced by disadvantaged students
The following are the potential barriers preventing the narrowing of the achievement gap between advantaged and disadvantaged pupils.
Social segregation
The academy is situated in Islington, which on average has measures of deprivation in the top 5% of most deprived areas in England. It is characterised by high levels of crime, acts of violence or anti-social behaviour, and high numbers of lone-parent families compared to national averages. As such, approximately 61% of pupils in Islington are eligible for FSM.
Attendance
Statistically, it has been proven that there is a clear link between poor attendance at school and lower academic achievement. Disadvantaged pupils are closely monitored by the pastoral team and the Attendance Officer, who will provide support to parents/carers in tackling issues affecting their child’s attendance or punctuality.
Parental engagement
Increasing the range of opportunities for parental involvement in the education of their children often has a positive impact on achievement. Where this is lacking, attainment levels often drop.
Effective feedback to parents/carers
Feedback needs to be constructively delivered in order to have a positive impact on achievement. The knowledge of what works and what doesn’t can often help to advance to better levels of understanding. Parental feedback when linked to learning objectives is often more effective in boosting student engagement.
Teaching quality
The maximisation of the impact of teaching is essential to ensuring that pupils are able to achieve at their highest potentials. Training interventions for teachers are essential to ensure effective teaching is consistently available to pupils.
Use of Pupil Premium in addressing the barriers (rationale of spend)
The Pupil Premium Grant will be utilised through a variety of targeted interventions which aim to improve the learning experiences of disadvantaged pupils:
One-to-one literacy, numeracy and science recovery
Behaviour mentor intervention programme
Engagement for students and families
Education welfare programme
Enrichment provision
Saturday school intervention programme
Half term and Easter revision courses
Boarding school and residential courses
Subsidised music tuition

pageCache.pageTitle: Careers Guidance for Parents - City of London Academy Highgate Hill
pageCache.text:
Careers Guidance for Parents
This section is provided to support parents in gaining a greater understanding of the world of work and careers in order to help their child at key decision points in Year 9 as they make their Option Choices and then again in Year 11 as they plan their post-16 progression. Finally, for those students that stay with us into 6th Form, we hope that the information provided will help parents to guide their child with the very important choices of courses and institutions for their further education provision at university and beyond.
Sign Up to a START PROFILE
As a parent, carer or guardian you play an important role in the career and education choices of your child. You have a huge amount of insight and experience to offer and Start can help you to understand how to do this effectively. It can also help you to update your own knowledge of the latest education and career pathways available to your child today. This is an invaluable resource equipped to help you, along with your child, to make well informed choices about future education and career pathways.
Please click on this link in order to get started – https://careers.startprofile.com/page/parents

pageCache.pageTitle: Fusion Skills & Career Ambassadors - City of London Academy Highgate Hill
pageCache.text:
Fusion Skills & Career Ambassadors
At Highgate Hill, we prioritise the holistic development of your children, emphasising Fusion Skills crucial for future success. Our focus includes excellent communication, creative thinking, problem-solving, collaboration, leadership, teamwork, and self-management skills.
We instil in students the importance of aiming high and staying positive, fostering a growth mindset. Our students develop Fusion Skills through their academic studies, enrichment opportunities, and the many trips we organise to support their learning in the classroom and their journey to becoming well-rounded individuals.
These skills, combined with the 4Cs (Communication, Creativity, Critical Thinking, and Collaboration), prepare our students for the dynamic demands of the job market. Effective communication, creative problem-solving, and collaborative teamwork are not just academic exercises, they are life skills.
We are pleased to introduce our Fusion Skills and Careers Ambassadors, who will play a crucial role in promoting transferable skills and supporting their peers in exploring career options. These students will act as a bridge between their classmates, teachers, and external organisations, helping to enhance employability and personal development for all year groups.
As ambassadors, they will engage in peer mentoring, organise careers events, and collaborate with staff and industry professionals to provide valuable resources and insights into various career pathways. Their contributions will be instrumental in fostering a supportive environment for skill development and career exploration within our school community.
